fifty-trillion-dollars.plain: Episode 1 asks where the money went. It follows the roughly $50 trillion that RAND researchers estimate moved from the bottom 90 percent of American households to the top 1 percent between 1975 and 2018.

the-ownership-class.plain: Episode 2 maps who sits at the top of the ownership of the American economy, sector by sector, drawing on public filings and reporting.

thirty-pipelines-one-destination.plain: Episode 3 lays out thirty mechanisms that move money upward, from housing and healthcare to debt and fees, and shows how they lead to the same place.

the-six-loops.plain: Episode 4 explains six feedback loops that keep the transfer of wealth going on its own, so that it continues even when individual actors change.

the-official-language.plain: Episode 5 compares what institutions say with what they do, translating common corporate and political language into its practical effect.

the-chair-not-the-sitter.plain: Episode 6 argues that the structure outlasts the person in charge: replacing a chief executive or official rarely changes outcomes when the role itself is built to extract.

the-enforcer.plain: Episode 7 looks at how the system's rules are carried home and enforced in ordinary life, through stress, debt and the stories people tell themselves.

the-body.plain: Episode 8 traces where economic pressure lands in the body: stress, chronic illness and the health effects of financial insecurity.

sarahs-tuesday.plain: A companion story that follows one ordinary person through one ordinary day, showing how the systems in the series touch every hour of it.

the-middle-tiers.plain: Episode 9 is addressed to the professionals in the middle tiers who keep the system running, and asks what happens when they stop cooperating.

the-differential.plain: Episode 10 shows where the extraction lands hardest: how race, disability, age, gender and geography change who carries the cost.

it-has-been-broken-before.plain: Episode 11 looks at times in history when concentrated economic power was successfully challenged, and what those movements had in common.

what-changes-at-every-scale.plain: Episode 12 is the action map: concrete steps at the level of a person, a household, a community and a country.
